text:
To determine the number of workers needed, we must calculate the effective capacity available for standard traffic after reserving a portion for spikes, and then divide the total request load by that effective capacity.

### Step 1: Calculate Effective Capacity per Worker

Each worker has a total capacity of 20 requests per second. However, 25% of this capacity must be reserved for spikes. Therefore, only 75% of the worker's capacity is available for the standard 120 requests per second.

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = \text{Total Capacity} \times (1 - \text{Spike Reserve})
$$

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = 20 \times (1 - 0.25)
$$

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = 20 \times 0.75 = 15 \text{ requests per second}
$$

### Step 2: Calculate Number of Workers Needed

Now, divide the total incoming request rate by the effective capacity per worker.

$$
\text{Workers Needed} = \frac{\text{Total Requests per Second}}{\text{Effective Capacity per Worker}}
$$
